__comment: The Park Bulletin (/now). One page per NPS Yosemite Guide edition: when the park publishes a new Guide (roughly every five weeks), rewrite this file from it, then (1) bump BULLETIN_URL's ?v= in page-now.jsx and HOME_BULLETIN_URL in page-home.jsx, (2) run `npm --prefix scripts run compile` and `npm --prefix scripts run seo`, (3) commit. edition.updated drives the /now sitemap lastmod, and edge/seo.js imports this file to serve the bulletin to non-JS crawlers. Facts come from the printed Guide plus the journal's own observation; do not carry a stale edition past its end date without a note. Event entries carry an `end` ISO date so the page can dim what has passed mid-edition. valleyDay rows carry optional `access` and `allAges` booleans: these are the printed Guide's own per-program symbols (wheelchair accessible / recommended for families), read off the Programs page row by row and never inferred, and they are true-only, because an unmarked program is one the Guide did not mark rather than one it ruled out. The same two marks ride on the PWA's program feed as `accessible` / `familyFriendly` (workers/src/data/manual-programs.ts); re-read both from the new Programs page each edition.

edition.label: August 19 – September 22, 2026
edition.lede: The edition where summer ends. Every road is still open and the high country is at its best, but the waterfalls are down to their bones and the park starts shutting for the season in the first two weeks of September: the High Sierra Camps, the pools, the Tuolumne store and grill, the hikers bus. Go high while you can.
edition.source: Condensed from the National Park Service Yosemite Guide for August 19 – September 22, 2026, with the journal's own notes.

alerts: The Mist Trail is closed for repairs Monday through Thursday, 7 am to 3:30 pm, through the end of October. It stays open Fridays, weekends, and holidays, and on weekdays before 7 am or after 3:30 pm when conditions allow. During the closure a signed detour on the John Muir Trail is the way to Vernal Fall, Nevada Fall, and everything beyond.

September is when the park closes down. Jennie's Ice Cream and the Wawona stable finish Sep 6; the Curry and Lodge pools Sep 7; the Tuolumne Meadows store and grill Sep 20. The High Sierra Camps at Glen Aulin and Sunrise close Sep 6 and May Lake Sep 9; Vogelsang and Merced Lake are closed all season.
The Tuolumne Meadows shuttle and the Tuolumne hikers bus both run only through Sep 13. After that the high country is drive-yourself.
Yosemite Falls is dry for the season and Mirror Lake is a meadow. Bridalveil, Vernal, and Nevada still run, thin. Go for the walls, not the water.
Wawona Hotel and its dining room are closed for renovation. White Wolf lodge, store, and dining room are closed this season.
Raft rentals on the Merced are done for the year.
EV charging in Tuolumne Meadows is temporarily unavailable. Charge in the Valley, El Portal, or Wawona.
Valley parking fills by late morning. Arrive before 8 am or after 4 pm, and text ynptraffic to 333111 for traffic alerts.

Climbing programs move back down to the Valley this edition: Ask-a-Climber restarts at El Capitan bridge Sep 6, and Climber Coffee returns to Camp 4 on Sep 13 after its last Tuolumne Sunday on Aug 30.

areas.name: Yosemite Valley
areas.note: Busy by mid-morning, worse on weekends, and quieter after Labor Day. Parking in three hubs: Curry Village, Yosemite Village, Yosemite Falls. Once parked, stay parked and ride the free shuttles.

areas.name: Tioga Road & Tuolumne Meadows
areas.note: The 39-mile high-country drive, 6,200 to nearly 10,000 feet. Little to no cell service; fuel and plan before you go. Store and grill close Sep 20, and the area shuttle stops Sep 13.

areas.name: Glacier Point Road
areas.note: One hour from the Valley. No trailers or vehicles over 30 feet past the Sentinel Dome trailhead. The gift shop runs 9 am to 7 pm.

areas.name: Wawona & Mariposa Grove
areas.note: An hour south of the Valley. Free grove shuttle every 15 minutes, 8 am to 7 pm, last bus down at 8 pm. The hotel is closed for renovation and the stable finishes Sep 6.

areas.name: Crane Flat
areas.note: Thirty minutes up Big Oak Flat Road, and the quiet way to see sequoias: Tuolumne Grove 2 miles round trip, Merced Grove 3. Information station and wilderness permits 8 am to 5 pm.

areas.name: Hetch Hetchy
areas.note: An hour and a half from the Valley. No services, very little shade, and hot into September. No vehicles or trailers over 25 feet long or 8 feet wide on the entrance road, and no pets on the dam or the trails.

areas.name: Gas
areas.note: El Portal 15 miles downhill on 140, Crane Flat 16.5 miles uphill on Big Oak Flat Road, Wawona 28 miles up Wawona Road. All pump 24 hours with a card.

Climber Coffee, from Sep 13

Ask-a-Climber, spotting scopes on El Cap, to 4:30 pm, from Sep 6
Paint & Sip watercolor, 2 hours, through Aug 28

Wee Wild Ones, kids 10 and under, through Sep 13
Movie Night

valleyDayNote: Everything unmarked is free and drop-in. Also running: the Valley Floor Tour by tram (10 am, 11 am, 1 pm, 2 pm, and sunset, ticketed), free photography walks from The Ansel Adams Gallery (Tu and Th 9 am, registration required) plus its paid field classes (smartphone photography W 9 am and Sa 1 pm, In the Footsteps of Ansel Adams M and Th 1 pm, digital-camera class Tu 1 pm), Conservancy art classes weekday mornings at 9 am, and the kids' open art studio at Happy Isles (10 am – 3 pm daily). The Mountaineering School's guided hikes start Sep 4: half-day walks to the Vernal Fall footbridge and around Mirror Lake on M, W, and Sa, full days to Nevada Fall on Tu and F and around El Capitan on Su and Th. Rows tagged wheelchair accessible or all ages carry the Yosemite Guide's own symbols for that program: accessible means it is held in a wheelchair-accessible facility or uses wheelchair-accessible paths, and the park asks you to raise any other accommodation with the program host. Of the extras above, the Valley Floor Tour is marked both and the kids' open art studio is marked accessible. An untagged program is one the Guide did not mark, not one it ruled out.

items: Bird walk W and Sa 7:30 am from Lembert Dome parking, binoculars available; coffee with a ranger Tu and Th 8 to 10 am at the campground's Dana circle; climber coffee Su 9 am at the store, last one Aug 30.

A walk leaves at 10 am every day: botany Su Tu from Lembert Dome, domes and meadows M Th from Parsons Lodge parking, geology W Sa from Pothole Dome, Tioga Pass botany F from Gaylor Lakes, junior rangers W Sa.
Parsons Memorial Lodge open daily 10 am – 4 pm at the Soda Springs, with an open reading room. Thirty-minute walk in from parking.
Welcome to Tuolumne!, a 15-minute orientation talk in the visitor center lot, noon and 3 pm daily.
Afternoon walks: the river W 1 pm from Dog Lake parking, forest M 2 pm, wildlife Th 2 pm from the visitor center, and the history walk on Aug 21 and 28 only.

Campfire program nightly 7:30 pm at the campground and a campfireside chat M W Sa 7:30 pm at the lodge, the latter only on nights the lodge is open. Stars Over Tuolumne M W Sa 9 pm from Lembert Dome parking; bring a pad and warm layers.

Marked wheelchair accessible in the Guide: climber coffee, both Welcome to Tuolumne! talks, the campground campfire, and the campfireside chat. Marked for all ages: those four, plus Parsons Lodge, the river, forest, and wildlife walks, and Stars Over Tuolumne.
Nothing runs in Wawona on Aug 19, the edition's first day. Everything below starts Aug 20.
Coffee with a ranger W and Su 9 am at Pine Tree Market. Bear talk with Ranger Jill W and Su 5 pm at The Redwoods fireside deck, free, kid and pet friendly, snacks provided.
Nature walk daily 9:30 am from the Mariposa Grove arrival area; junior ranger talk daily 1:30 pm in the grove, for kids 4 and up. Allow time to park and ride the shuttle up first.
Campfire program nightly 7 pm at the Wawona campground amphitheater, back on the schedule after an edition off.
Mariposa Grove Depot 9 am – 5 pm. The Yosemite History Center's outdoor exhibits are open daily.
Stable rides F – W at 8 am, 11 am, and 3 pm, all-day ride Th at 8 am, pony rides 10:30 am – 3 pm, all finishing Sep 6. The 1918 golf course is open 8 am – 6 pm; book at the Wawona Store.
Marked wheelchair accessible in the Guide: coffee with a ranger and the bear talk, the bear talk for all ages as well. The Mariposa Grove walks and the campfire carry no mark either way.
Giant sequoia hike M W Th 11 am in the Tuolumne Grove, a mile down from the trailhead, 2.5 miles and 500 feet round trip. Junior ranger table daily 2 – 3:30 pm at the trailhead.

Evening program Su W Th F Sa 6:30 pm at the Crane Flat campground amphitheater, none on Aug 22 or 23. Stars Over Crane Flat 8 pm on Sep 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 12: free, but register at the Big Oak Flat Information Station. No pets, RVs, or trailers.

Glacier Point Starry Skies 9 pm, ticketed, on Aug 19 and 20, Sep 6 through 10, and Sep 13 through 17 only. Transportation up is on you, and it is an hour from the Valley in the dark. The free astronomy-club star parties that ran through mid-August are not on this edition's schedule.

Marked wheelchair accessible in the Guide: the junior ranger table, the Crane Flat evening program, and Glacier Point Starry Skies. Marked for all ages: the sequoia hike, the evening program, Stars Over Crane Flat, and Starry Skies.

events.title: Stewardship Series: Tuolumne Meadows Overview
events.note: Conservancy stewardship series. Register at Yosemite.org; free for donors.

events.title: Junior Ranger Day
events.note: Special drop-in programs all over the park. Ask at any information center. In the Mariposa Grove the 1:30 pm talk meets in the parking area today.

events.title: Moonlight Tour
events.note: Two-hour tram tour of the Valley under a nearly full moon. Ticketed at TravelYosemite.com. Wheelchair accessible and marked for all ages. Runs again Sep 22.

events.title: Yosemite Art Trail
events.note: A week of art-themed drop-in programs and hands-on activities. Ask at an information center for the day's locations.

events.title: Tom Killion: Trails and Trees
events.where: The Ansel Adams Gallery, 9 am – 5 pm
events.note: Sierra woodblocks and prints. Free to walk through.

events.title: Poetry from Tahoe to Yosemite
events.note: Chris Olander, poet laureate and ecology bio-educator. Free, all ages. Very limited parking: ride the shuttle to stop 12.

events.title: Legacy of the Old Yosemite Village
events.note: Alice van Ommeren, author of Yosemite's Historic Hotels and Camps. Free, all ages.

events.title: Mystery Cat: Yosemite's Elusive Mountain Lion
events.note: Don Endicott, Anza-Borrego Desert State Park. Free, all ages.

events.title: Amazing World of Bats
events.note: Don Endicott again, on the park's tiny fighter jets. Free, all ages.

events.title: Moonlight Tour
events.note: The season's last one. Ticketed at TravelYosemite.com. Wheelchair accessible and marked for all ages.

eventsNote: Conservancy art classes run weekday mornings at 9 am at Happy Isles (register at Yosemite.org/art): watercolor nature journaling with Sylvia Eneriz through Aug 21, watercolor with Jessica de Jesus Aug 24 – 28, pastels with Miranda Craft Aug 31 – Sep 4, printmaking with Leah Petersen Sep 7 – 11, watercolor with Steve Curl Sep 14 – 18. Looking just past this edition: the Yosemite Facelift, the park's biggest volunteer cleanup, runs Sep 23 – 27 out of the Valley, free with registration at yosemiteclimbing.org.

trails.name: Mist Trail to Vernal & Nevada Falls
trails.note: Closed M – Th, 7 am – 3:30 pm for repairs through the end of October; open F – Su, holidays, and outside those hours when conditions allow. Use the signed John Muir Trail detour during the closure. Footbridge 1.6 mi and 380 ft round trip, top of Vernal 2.4 mi and 1,000 ft, top of Nevada 5 mi and 2,000 ft; the Clark Point loop back on the John Muir Trail makes those 3.7 and 5.8 miles. All of it from Happy Isles, shuttle stop 16.

trails.name: Half Dome
trails.note: Cables are up, which means a permit every day of the week, and they typically come down in the first half of October. Daily lottery two days ahead on Recreation.gov, applications midnight to 4 pm. 14 to 16 miles and 4,800 feet: be honest about the day.

trails.name: Lower Yosemite Fall
trails.note: 1 mi loop, shuttle stop 6, east side wheelchair-accessible. The fall is done for the season and returns with the first autumn storms. Go for the amphitheater and the scale of the wall.

trails.name: Mirror Lake
trails.note: 2 mi round trip and 100 ft on the paved road, shuttle stop 17, or 4.5 mi around the basin on the unpaved trail. The lakebed is a meadow this time of year. Leashed pets on the paved road only; a valid disability placard may drive it.

trails.name: Bridalveil Fall
trails.note: 0.5 mi paved from the parking area to a wheelchair-accessible viewing area, steeper to the base. Thin but still showing in the afternoon wind. Stay behind the barriers: the rocks at the base are slick.

trails.name: Cook's Meadow
trails.note: 1 mi flat loop of pavement and boardwalk, shuttle stop 6. Half Dome and Yosemite Falls views; best light early and late, and the birds are out at both ends of the day.

trails.name: Yosemite Falls Trail
trails.note: Columbia Rock, 2 mi round trip, earns the view. Full climb 7.2 mi and 2,700 ft, six to eight hours, dozens of switchbacks, start at dawn. From Camp 4, shuttle stop 7.

trails.name: Four Mile Trail
trails.note: 9.6 mi and 3,200 ft round trip to Glacier Point, six to eight hours, from shuttle stop 11. One-way option: ride the tour bus up, walk down. Drop-offs only at the point, no pickup.

trails.name: Valley Loop Trail
trails.note: Up to 11.5 mi, mostly flat but uneven, and the quietest miles on the floor. No pets or bikes.

trails.name: Sentinel Dome & Taft Point
trails.note: One trailhead on Glacier Point Road, two rim walks: Taft Point 2.4 mi round trip west, Sentinel Dome 1.8 mi northeast.

trails.name: Tuolumne & Merced Groves
trails.note: The uncrowded sequoias, both near Crane Flat: Tuolumne Grove 2 mi round trip with a 500 ft climb out, Merced Grove 3 mi with 520 ft. You walk down first, so save the legs for the return.

trailsNote: Overnights require a wilderness permit year-round, and a bear canister; rent one at permit pickup. Carry a quart of water per person for every two hours, three for the falls corridor, plus salty snacks, a headlamp, a map, and a layer. Turn around when half the water is gone. No pets or bikes on any hiking trail. Big-wall climbers self-register for overnight permits at the kiosk near shuttle stop 9.

transit.name: Valley shuttles
transit.note: Free, daily 7 am – 10 pm, year-round. Valleywide green line hits every stop, every 22 – 32 minutes, an hour and a half round trip; the purple East Valley line runs every 18 – 22 minutes, 50 minutes round trip. No pets.

transit.name: Mariposa Grove shuttle
transit.note: Free, every 15 minutes, 8 am – 7 pm; last bus leaves the grove at 8 pm. No ticket needed.

transit.name: Tuolumne Meadows shuttle
transit.note: Free, between the Meadows and Olmsted Point, 8 am – 4 pm, but only through Sep 13.

transit.name: Hiker buses
transit.note: Tuolumne hikers bus once daily through Sep 13; the Glacier Point tour bus twice daily, a four-hour trip. Both paid, both bookable at TravelYosemite.com or the Lodge front desk. Glacier Point drops hikers one-way; no pickup at the point.

transit.name: YARTS
transit.note: Public transit into the park: Merced year-round with multiple departures; Sonora two or three times daily, Fresno and Mammoth Lakes twice daily, all summer only. YARTS.com or 877/989-2787.

transit.name: Bikes
transit.note: Over 11 miles of paved path on the Valley floor, 15 mph limit, helmets required under 18, and no bikes on hiking trails. Rentals 8 am – 7 pm at the Lodge, Curry Village, and Yosemite Village, 9 am – 6 pm from Sep 8; free bike share for one- to two-hour rides from the Village and Camp 4 lots, goyose.org/bikeshare.

transit.name: EV charging
transit.note: Level 2 only: Curry Village (20), Wawona Store (24), Yosemite Falls parking (10), the Lodge (8), The Ahwahnee (6), Welcome Center (4), El Portal (2). Tuolumne chargers are down.

essentials.title: Bears
essentials.text: Food storage is federal law: within arm's reach by day, out of the car and into a locker by night, and never in a truck bed or strapped to the outside. To a bear, food means anything with a scent, trash and toiletries included. Twenty-seven bears were hit by vehicles here last year, so hold the speed limit at dawn and dusk. Sightings: 209/372-0322.

essentials.title: Lightning
essentials.text: Afternoon thunderstorms run into September. Off the domes and exposed rim when storms build; shelter in a building or vehicle.

essentials.title: Smoke & fire
essentials.text: Fire season runs from here into October, and this is usually its worst stretch. Check air quality at fire.airnow.gov the morning you drive in, not the night before. Fires only in portable stoves, grills, and established rings, never unattended, and out cold before you walk away.

essentials.title: Wildlife
essentials.text: 150 feet from bears and coyotes, 25 feet from everything else. Feeding or approaching any animal is illegal, birds and squirrels included.

essentials.title: Heat & water
essentials.text: The Valley floor is still hot by late morning through early September, and Hetch Hetchy is worse. Walk early, carry a quart per person per two hours, and move uphill by noon. Nights in Tuolumne are cold year-round: pack a real layer.

essentials.title: Parking
essentials.text: Designated spaces or paved turnouts only, pulled fully off the road. Vehicles on vegetation get cited and towed.

essentials.title: Pets
essentials.text: Not allowed on trails, on shuttles, or inside buildings. Leashed on paved roads, paved bike paths, and the Mirror Lake road. Service dogs go anywhere visitors go; emotional support and therapy animals follow the pet rules.

essentials.title: The rules with teeth
essentials.text: Prohibited: drones, feeding or approaching wildlife, collecting plants, animals, or arrowheads, hunting, metal detectors, driving into meadows, biking off pavement, camping outside a designated campground, weapons inside federal buildings, and marijuana of any kind.

essentials.title: Camping
essentials.text: Every campground needs a reservation: Recreation.gov or 877/444-6777. Sleeping in a vehicle is legal only at a site you have booked, never at a roadside or in a parking lot.

essentials.title: Navigation
essentials.text: GPS gives wrong directions inside the park and routes people onto closed roads. Follow the road signs. There is no usable signal for most of Tioga Road or Glacier Point Road.

essentials.title: Wifi
essentials.text: Free at Degnan's Kitchen and the Mariposa County Library in the Valley, the El Portal Market, and the Wawona library. Hotel guests get it at the Lodge, Curry Village, and The Ahwahnee.
